response:
*leans back, turns a small wooden figure over in my hands*

All the pieces matter. Let me tell you what I see.

This ain't about SmartSync. This is about a CEO who got excited at a conference and made a promise they can't keep. The CTO knows it's impossible - that's why they went silent. Sarah knows it. Raj knows it. Everyone knows it except maybe Alex, and that boy's enthusiasm is gonna get him hurt if we don't protect him.

**First, I'm talking to Sarah straight:**

"Sarah, I can help you, but not by pretending this is buildable. Here's what we do: You're gonna write a PRD, but you're gonna write *two versions*. First one is what the CEO described - full SmartSync, 3-month timeline, realistic. Second one is what we can actually demo in 2 weeks - a focused proof-of-concept. One core feature, polished. Let leadership choose. You're not saying no. You're giving options. That's your job."

**In planning, here's what I tell my team:**

"Look, we ain't burning down for vaporware. We're gonna plan what we *can* build. We identify the single most impressive thing that's actually achievable - something we can demo with pride. Jamie's right about cutting scope. We figure out what slice of this shows the vision without killing ourselves. Casey gets their three days. Lin, I hear you - no crunch. We do honest work, honest hours."

**On escalation:**

I'm not going around anyone. But I'm documenting everything. Every conversation, every impossible ask, every timeline we flagged. Brick by brick, I build the case. Not to blame - to protect. When this goes sideways, and it will, there's a paper trail showing we raised concerns and offered alternatives.

**The sprint itself:**

We plan for what we control. Proof-of-concept. One feature that actually works. Clean demo. If leadership wants the full vision, they need to give us the timeline or resources. That's the message Raj carries up the chain, because Tech Leads have that standing.

**What am I sacrificing?**

Not my team's health. Not their weekends. Not their trust. 

I'm sacrificing the comfortable lie. I'm sacrificing being the "yes man" the CEO probably wants. Maybe I'm sacrificing some political capital. But a case built on lies falls apart. A team run into the ground doesn't recover. 

The CEO might not get their demo. Sarah might still get blamed - I can't control that, but I can give her a fighting chance with options instead of paralysis. The CTO might stay silent forever.

But my team? My team walks out of this with their integrity. And when the dust settles, when the next impossible thing comes down, they'll know I had their backs.

*sets down the wooden figure*

That's how we play this. Follow the money, follow the timeline, follow the truth. All the pieces matter.
